doc.title: Laurence Juber interviewed by Monk Rowe, Glasgow, Scotland, July 27, 2016 [interview 1 of 2]

title: Teenage versatility, NYJO camps and studying classical guitar for college
summary: He took any gig, studied classical guitar through Grade 8, attended National Youth Jazz Orchestra camps, and was accepted at Leeds.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: Did you get a reputation in the studio for a certain style?

I was a versatile guy. I mean if they needed a banjo I’d go and borrow a banjo for the session. But because I understood the nature of the versatility. Now as a teenager I was playing with rock bands as well as doing the money stuff. And I mean making five pounds for a gig was a lot better than babysitting or washing my neighbor’s car, although if I washed my neighbor’s car I got tickets for Tottenham Hotspur’s games, which was the local soccer team. So it was worth it. But I was doing a lot of stuff. I mean as soon as I was able to I started going to National Youth Jazz Orchestra camps and hooked up with an alto sax player and he and I would go — I was probably about 18 at the time. He and I would go and play gigs where we had no repertoire, we would just improvise for a whole gig, just like riffing and grooving. Any musical experience was happy for me. So I was studying classical guitar. I took that up to Grade 8, because I needed it in order to study music. I took Grade 5 classical guitar so I could do A level music. I took Grade 8 so I would be able to go to college. And by the time I left high school I knew I wanted to be a studio musician. I got accepted at Leeds College of Music in the North of England, which was the closest thing we had to the Berklee School of Music, as far as you could actually study jazz and you could study all that stuff there, versus going to one of the conservatories for example. But when I got better exam grades than I expected, in fact my music teachers were shocked that I got an A in music. Because I was kind of on the hooligan side as far as I wasn’t legit.
